title: K-flatness of the canonical open restriction of a complex
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], U an arbitrary open, and P an unbounded complex of O_X-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let R be the over-site restriction followed by the canonical over equivalence to O_U-modules [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]. If P is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex], then its termwise restriction R(P) is K-flat over O_U. No flatness of individual terms or boundedness is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 20.26.8, specialized to the inclusion of an open; stalk criterion Tag 06YB

proof.text: Apply the stalk criterion to P on X to obtain K-flatness of every stalk complex.

For x in U, neighborhoods in X contained in U are cofinal among neighborhoods of its image. Thus the restriction-section identifications yield a stalk-ring isomorphism and a natural identification of restricted module stalks. Naturality identifies all differentials. Transport modules along the ring isomorphism; this equivalence preserves acyclicity and identifies balanced tensor products, hence their direct-sum total complexes. It therefore transports K-flatness of the original stalk to that of the restricted stalk.
Use the stalk criterion on U to conclude. For U empty the quantification over stalks is vacuous.
